"Upgrade Flow: change request and waves"

Stages 2 and 3 of the Upgrade Flow — raise one change request (or one per wave) that cites the pre-upgrade evidence of every appliance in the window, then drive that change without leaving the page.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereAutomation → Upgrade Flow, cards 2 and 3 (URL /web/upgrade-flow/ — form posts to /web/upgrade-flow/change and /web/upgrade-flow/waves)

What is it?#

Stage 2 of the Upgrade Flow raises one change request of the built-in upgrade type for the appliances you ticked in stage 1, citing the pre-upgrade run you chose for each of them. Alternatively it splits the same selection into waves, one ordinary change request per wave. Once a change is raised, stage 3 shows that change in full on the same page so you can approve, schedule, notify and export it without leaving the flow.

What does it do?#

  • Uses the same form and the same creation rules as Change Requests → New, with three differences: the change type is fixed to the upgrade type, the affected devices are the ones ticked in stage 1 (read-only here), and you come back to the flow afterwards.
  • Proposes the Title, Reason and Rollback plan from the wording set for the upgrade type under Administration → Change Types, with the ticked appliance names substituted in.
  • Derives the change's destination version from the cited runs and stores it on the change.
  • Binds every cited run to the change, and freezes the affected-service inventory onto it.
  • In waves mode, creates up to 12 changes, each with its own window and approval, titled <title> — wave k/N.

Requirements#

  • At least one appliance ticked in stage 1. Citing a pre-upgrade run is optional per appliance, but an appliance without one carries no baseline.
  • The built-in upgrade change type must be enabled under Administration → Change Types; otherwise the card shows "The change type this flow raises is disabled in Administration → Change Types, so no change can be raised from here. Re-enable it there." with an Open change type link.
  • All ticked appliances must be FortiWeb: the upgrade change type runs against FortiWeb only. Stage 1 lists only FortiWeb appliances, so this holds for any selection made on the page (see Troubleshooting).

Permissions#

  • Stages 2 and 3 are rendered only for users with users.manage (Administrator). Users who can open the flow with the backup permissions alone do not see these cards; a direct POST returns 403.
  • Every lifecycle button in stage 3 (Approve, Schedule, Mark notified, Edit, Cancel CR, the external-record buttons) also requires users.manage.

How to use#

Raise one change for the window#

  1. Tick the appliances and choose their evidence in stage 1 (see Upgrade Flow).
  2. In card 2 — Change request (CRQ), check the header: it shows Upgrade to <version> derived from the ticked runs, "Two destinations ticked: …" if the runs disagree, and "N appliance(s) cite no destination".
  3. Document language — pick the language of the change document (required; pre-selected from your profile language if one is set).
  4. Type of change — fixed to the upgrade type and shown disabled. Set Risk (Low, Medium, High; default Medium).
  5. Proposed wording — review Title (required), Reason and Rollback plan. Fields marked auto still follow the proposal; once you edit a field it is never overwritten. Restore proposal re-applies the proposal; Edit this wording opens the change type.
  6. Set Change owner (Verantwortlicher) (pre-filled with your user name), Notify on completion (pre-filled with the default email recipient) and Approval: Manual — approved here in SATOM or External — an integration must approve it.
  7. Scope & window — Affected devices mirrors the stage 1 ticks and cannot be edited here. Set Window start and Window end in the console timezone shown beside the label.
  8. Click Create draft. The button stays disabled until at least one appliance is ticked ("Tick at least one appliance in step 1."), and the server refuses a change without appliances as well.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a change without appliances is refused ("Pick at least one appliance for the change. Nothing was created."), and FortiADC appliances are no longer offered in stage 1, so they can no longer reach this stage.

Split the selection into waves#

  1. Below the form, under Or split the same selection into waves, set: - Appliances per wave (default 5) - First window start (optional) - Window (minutes) (default 120) - Gap in minutes between windows (default 30)
  2. Click Raise one change per wave.

Appliances are chunked in name order. Each wave reuses the title, reason, rollback, document language, risk, owner, notification address and approval mode from the form above. Windows are consecutive and never overlap. Leave the start empty to raise the waves without windows and schedule them later.

Work with the raised change (stage 3)#

After Create draft the flow reloads citing the change (?cr=<id>):

  • Card 2 folds under a Raised as <ref> badge; Show what was submitted (read-only) reveals the inputs. Submitting again is not possible from the folded card — a second submission would raise a second change.
  • Card 3 shows the change itself: its destination (Upgrade to <version> or no destination recorded on this change), status, the action bar (Approve, Schedule/Re-schedule, Mark notified, Edit, Cancel CR), the overview, the change document, Affected services with the per-appliance evidence table and Download .xlsx / .csv export, the external change record, the timeline and the maintenance notice. Each button returns you to the flow.
  • Continue with card 4 to plan the rollout — see rollout and execution.

To raise a change for the next group of appliances, open Upgrade Flow again from the menu (without the ?cr= link). Stage 3 is shown only for the change the link names; a plain visit shows no change.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Document language Language of the change document and proposed text Yes EN
Risk low / medium / high No (medium) High
Title Change title (max 200 characters stored) Yes Upgrade fweb-01, fweb-02 to 8.0.5
Reason Printed in the change document No Vendor security fix
Rollback plan Printed in the change document No Boot the previous partition
Change owner (Verantwortlicher) Accountable person; printed in §1 No (pre-filled) jdoe
Notify on completion Who is emailed when the window closes No ops@example.com
Approval Manual or External (fail-closed) No (Manual) Manual
Window start / Window end Maintenance window, console timezone, stored as UTC No (needed later to schedule) 2026-10-10 22:00 / 2026-10-11 02:00
Appliances per wave Waves only Yes for waves 5
First window start Waves only; wave 1's window start No 2026-10-10 22:00
Window (minutes) Waves only; length of each wave window No (120) 90
Gap Waves only; minutes between wave windows No (30) 30

Example#

🧪Example — Twelve FortiWeb appliances in three waves

You ticked 12 appliances, each citing a clean run towards 8.0.5. With Appliances per wave = 5, First window start = 22:00, Window (minutes) = 120 and Gap = 30, Raise one change per wave creates:

Change Appliances Window
… — wave 1/3 first 5 by name 22:00–00:00
… — wave 2/3 next 5 00:30–02:30
… — wave 3/3 last 2 03:00–05:00

Flash: "3 wave(s) raised over 12 appliance(s). Each is an ordinary change request: approve, schedule and execute them one at a time." The waves appear under Batched rollouts.

Result#

  • Single change: a change request in draft with the ticked appliances, the cited runs bound to it, the destination version (when the cited runs declare one), and a frozen inventory of affected services. Flash: "Change request <ref> "<title>" was raised. Approve and schedule it from the change itself; this flow now cites it." Audit entries change_request.create and upgrade_flow.change.
  • Waves: N draft change requests sharing a batch reference, each knowing its wave index; the page lists them under Batched rollouts (up to the five newest batches, only waves visible to you), each wave linking to its execution progress page. Audit entry upgrade_flow.waves.
  • If a single change is refused, the same page is re-rendered with the refusal and everything you entered — wording, owner, notification, approval mode, window as typed, ticks and the run cited per appliance. A refused waves request redirects back to an unfilled form.

Troubleshooting#

"A title is required."#

Possible causes - The Title field is empty.

Solution 1. Type a title or click Restore proposal, then Create draft.

Verification - The success flash names the change reference.

"Pick at least one appliance for the change. Nothing was created."#

Possible causes - The form was posted with no appliance ticked in stage 1.

Solution 1. Tick the appliances in stage 1, then Create draft again.

Verification - The success flash names the change reference.

Does not run against fortiadc#

The flash reads "<change type label> does not run against fortiadc (<names>). It supports: fortiweb."

Possible causes - A posted selection named FortiADC appliances (stage 1 no longer lists them). The upgrade change type acts on FortiWeb only, because SATOM has no firmware flash path for FortiADC.

Solution 1. Reload the flow and tick FortiWeb appliances only. Run the FortiADC pre-upgrade from the appliance page (see Firmware upgrade).

Verification - The change is raised.

"The pre-upgrade runs cited here were run towards different versions (…). One change request is one move"#

Possible causes - The runs selected in Evidence this change cites were swept towards different destinations (the header shows Two destinations ticked).

Solution 1. Cite runs swept towards the same version, or raise one change per destination.

Verification - The card header shows a single Upgrade to <version> badge.

"The maintenance window ends at or before it starts, so no instant lies inside it and the change could never fire. Nothing was created."#

Possible causes - Window end is equal to or earlier than Window start.

Solution 1. Correct the window and submit again (your inputs are kept).

Verification - The change is raised and its overview shows the window.

"One or more selected devices do not exist or are not visible to you. Nothing was created."#

Possible causes - A ticked appliance was removed, put into maintenance mode or belongs to another ADOM.

Solution 1. Reload the page and tick the appliances again.

Verification - The change is raised.

"upgrade is not a change-controlled action."#

Possible causes - The upgrade change type was disabled under Administration → Change Types after the page loaded.

Solution 1. Re-enable it there (Open change type), then reload the flow.

Verification - Card 2 shows the form instead of the disabled notice.

"Wave N was refused: … N wave(s) had already been created — open Change Requests and remove them before retrying."#

Possible causes - One wave failed the same rules as a single change (for example an appliance that became invisible to you after the page loaded). Earlier waves were already created.

Solution 1. Open Change Requests and cancel the waves already created. 2. Fix the cause and raise the waves again.

Verification - Batched rollouts shows one complete batch.

"… is N waves; at most 12 are created at once."#

Possible causes - The selection divided by Appliances per wave exceeds 12.

Solution 1. Raise Appliances per wave or split the selection. Nothing was created.

Verification - The waves are raised.

Other waves refusals#

  • "Select at least one appliance to build waves from." — tick appliances in stage 1.
  • "Set how many appliances go in each wave." — enter Appliances per wave ≥ 1.
  • "The waves need a title. It is proposed from the change type — restore it or write your own. Nothing was created." — fill Title in the form above.

Advanced#

Advanced How the destination reaches the change

The create form posts no destination of its own. The change takes the destination declared by the cited runs; if they declare two, the change is refused. A change citing no run that declares a destination records none, and stage 3 says no destination recorded on this change.

Advanced Which run is cited

Each run is accepted only for an appliance in the change, and each appliance's coverage is its first bound run. The first run bound becomes the change's primary citation and is never re-pointed. Appliances without a bound run are listed as having no baseline on the change and on the execution page.

Advanced Visibility

A ?cr= id naming a change you cannot see (no visible appliance) is ignored silently — the page renders as a plain visit, never a 404.
